header:
Date: 2027-12-02
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Jenna Ortiz (Redwood AE); Marcus Lee (Redwood SE); Priya Raman (Zephyr Head of ML); Daniel Ortiz (Zephyr Cloud Infra); Sofie Müller (Zephyr Security); Tom Yang (Zephyr Product); Lina (Zephyr Eng)
summary: POC scoping lab to pick deployment lane for Zephyr Intelligence's document ingestion and Q&A feature. Discussed success criteria (latency percentile targets, cost per 1k tokens, uptime), workload sizing, bench plan, and timeline. Major constraints: EU data residency, SOC2 auditors, bursty batch inference at night. Team aligned to run a three-model benchmark across Hosted/Dedicated/Private prototypes and reconvene for decision review.
topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs; private/on-prem feasibility; security/compliance requirements; pilot timeline and acceptance criteria
transcript:
00:00 Jenna Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we have about 50 minutes, we'll focus on the decision lane and concrete acceptance criteria. Marcus and I will capture bench plan and next steps.
00:18 Priya Raman: Thanks, quick context — we're building a doc ingestion + conversational Q&A feature across EU and US customers. Throughput peaks are weird, daytime web traffic around 50 RPS but nightly batch inference spikes to 500 RPS for re-embedding. Latency sensitivity for interactive is P95 <= 250ms target.
00:40 Marcus Lee: Got it. P95 250ms is ambitious, we'll need to see model choice and sequence lengths; that target can be met on dedicated hardware usually, hosted can as well depending on model and batching.
00:58 Daniel Ortiz: Security's the main ask — EU-only residency for PII, SOC2 is table stakes. We'll likely require VPC peering or an on-prem option for the most sensitive datasets.
01:12 Sofie Müller: And KMS integration; our auditors want envelope encryption and logs. Does Redwood's Private option support customer-managed keys?
01:24 Jenna Ortiz: Yes, private supports KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include the security pack. For Hosted we offer encrypted at rest and BYOK in dedicated plans — we'll share specifics.
01:38 Tom Yang: For success criteria, Priya and I sketched: P95 latency <=250ms for conversational queries, median <=80ms; embedding batch throughput 500 items/min with acceptable failure 0.1% and cost target of under $0.02 per API call. Also rollout timeline: pilot in 6 weeks.
02:00 Priya Raman: Right, and acceptance: ability to failover without >1 minute customer-visible outage and regression tests on a 200 prompt eval set.
02:15 Marcus Lee: Good. Let's map those to deployment lanes. Hosted: fastest to spin up, easiest for rapid pilot, predictable for small-scale, but data-residency nuances — Redwood can pin region, but for strict EU-only PII there may be policy papers to sign. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in a region, predictable latency and cost; supports BYOK and custom autoscale rules. Private: full VPC/on-prem — addresses residency and audits but longer lead time.
02:45 Lina: Curious on autoscaling — how quickly does Dedicated scale for short night spikes? We have very spiky batch windows.
02:52 Marcus Lee: Dedicated supports burst pools and pre-warmed nodes; scaling is policy driven. For very short spikes we recommend async queues or using burst capacity to avoid cold starts. We'll capture sample policies.
03:08 Daniel Ortiz: For Private, what's the typical lead time? We can't be blocked for months.
03:12 Jenna Ortiz: Private on-prem baseline can be 6-10 weeks depending on connectivity and security review; a VPC-hosted private control plane is usually 3-4 weeks. For this pilot, the combination most customers pick is start Hosted for functional validation, run parallel Dedicated bench for performance and legal validation, and if Private is required escalate post-pilot.
03:37 Tom Yang: That matches our risk appetite. We want to validate model quality and interactive latency quickly, then make a final hosting decision tied to SOC2 signoff.
03:50 Marcus Lee: On benchmarks — we propose a three-model matrix: small/fast embedding model, mid-size chat model (e.g., 7B) and a larger 70B decoder for worst-case latency. We'll run: 1) interactive single-user P95 latency test (50 concurrent sessions simulating real prompts), 2) burst batch throughput test (500 qps for 10 minutes), 3) sustained 1k token-per-second throughput to measure token cost.
04:18 Priya Raman: We'll provide 10 representative prompts and 2 weeks of traces; we have a sample corpus and a redaction step so you can run against non-PII variant for Hosted.
04:31 Jenna Ortiz: Perfect. Marcus will run those with three hosting configs: Hosted (region EU-West), Dedicated (3-GPU pool in EU-West with 2x burst reserve), Private (if allowed, we'll spin a trimmed on-prem sim with same kernel stack). Each run we'll measure P50/P95/P99 latencies, token cost, and throughput.
05:00 Sofie Müller: For the security pack, can you annotate any known residuals in Hosted where logs might traverse US? Our legal team will need that.
05:10 Jenna Ortiz: We'll annotate exactly what crosses what boundary. Redwood keeps control plane metadata in multi-region but we can get a region-specific data flow diagram for EU-only options.
05:20 Priya Raman: On quality, we also need a comparison on any quantized model performance impacts — does Dedicated/Private give us different quantization options?
05:28 Marcus Lee: Dedicated and Private let you use more aggressive quantization and custom kernels with slightly different perf/quality tradeoffs. Hosted offers curated quantization profiles; worst-case you can end up with small quality drift, we'll include eval metrics.
05:45 Tom Yang: Cost — can you ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated for our projected 2M tokens/month baseline?
05:50 Jenna Ortiz: We'll produce a TCO sheet; quick rule of thumb: Hosted is higher per-token but lower ops overhead; Dedicated reduces per-token by ~30-45% at committed usage; Private has higher fixed cost and lower marginal cost but needs infra ops. We'll put numbers in the follow-up.
06:10 Daniel Ortiz: One more constraint: our legal team wants to avoid adding long-term vendor risk. If we go Dedicated with reserved nodes, what are exit strategies?
06:20 Jenna Ortiz: You can export KV cache and snapshots; Redwood supports model variant pinning and we can provide handover runbooks. We also avoid lock-in by using standard model formats (HF/ggml variations depending on model). We'll detail the handover steps.
06:34 Marcus Lee: Ok for the bench harness we'll need: two weeks of traces, sample prompts, target SLAs, and a list of models you want included. Priya, do you have model preferences?
06:45 Priya Raman: We're leaning to a 7B strong chat model for prod and a 13B for fallback; embeddings using a mid-cost model. Include an LLM approx latency baseline for both.
06:56 Marcus Lee: Noted. We'll include the fallback variants too.
07:03 Lina: A practical question — how do you measure P95 when you have caching in play? Our interactive system can hit prefix cache which artifically lowers latency.
07:12 Marcus Lee: We'll run cold-cache and warmed-cache passes. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache emission so bench will include both. We'll annotate which percent of calls hit the cache.
07:25 Tom Yang: Regarding canary and rollouts — if we pick Dedicated, can we A/B traffic to Hosted fallback?
07:31 Jenna Ortiz: Yes, Redwood routing policies support region/model/route-based fallback. You can do canary traffic and automatic fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is exhausted.
07:44 Sofie Müller: Audit logging — we need immutable logs for 12 months. Does Redwood provide append-only logs or will we need to ship logs to our SIEM?
07:53 Marcus Lee: You can retain logs in Redwood for configurable retention and also stream to your SIEM. For compliance, many customers push audit logs into their own GCS/S3 buckets.
08:06 Daniel Ortiz: Networking — what options for private connectivity? VPC peering, PrivateLink, VPN?
08:12 Jenna Ortiz: All three; Private supports direct connect patterns if on-prem. We'll include sample network diagrams in the security pack.
08:22 Priya Raman: Ok, timeline check. If we start bench now, how long until we can make a hosting decision and go into a 6-week pilot?
08:30 Jenna Ortiz: Bench runs take 3-7 days depending on queueing — say one week for initial bench and 3 days for analysis. Then decision review 1 week after bench. So pilot kickoff could be in 3 weeks if all materials are ready. Private on-prem ramp would add extra weeks.
08:48 Marcus Lee: We'll aim for bench results by 2027-12-09 as we discussed.
09:00 Priya Raman: On acceptance tests — we want automated regression on the 200 prompt eval set and a soak test for 48 hours at 2x expected peak traffic.
09:10 Marcus Lee: Soak test noted; we'll recommend a staging cluster for soak to avoid affecting prod.
09:18 Tom Yang: What about data retention and deletion policies? We need proof we can support right-to-be-forgotten requests.
09:26 Sofie Müller: Yes legal requires deletion APIs and proof of deletion.
09:30 Jenna Ortiz: Redwood provides retention controls and deletion endpoints. For private/on-prem, customer fully controls data lifecycle. We'll include sample deletion audit trails.
09:45 Lina: A little nit — model updates and rollouts. If Redwood upgrades the underlying model version, how do we prevent sudden regressions?
09:52 Marcus Lee: Redwood has rollout policies and you can pin model versions in route configs. We'll also run evaluations against your prompt set and only allow promoted model versions after passing quality gates.
10:08 Priya Raman: Can we do an initial micro-pilot on Hosted limited to non-PII EU data while we run Dedicated bench? That would let product iterate quickly.
10:17 Jenna Ortiz: Absolutely — many customers do that. Hosted in EU region using redacted dataset typically works for the initial eval. Then you can shift to Dedicated or Private for production depending on bench.
10:30 Daniel Ortiz: For the Dedicated config you suggested earlier — 3 GPUs with 2x burst reserve — can you share expected P95 numbers for a 7B model?
10:38 Marcus Lee: Ballpark: warmed cache P95 could be under 150ms for 7B on a 3-GPU shard if kernels and batching align. Cold-cache or long context could push to 300-400ms. We'll quantify in bench results.
10:54 Tom Yang: Any licensing or egress fees we should be aware of?
11:00 Jenna Ortiz: That's model-dependent and we'll call out egress for multi-region use; also some enterprise features (longer observability retention, extended SLAs) are add-ons.
11:12 Priya Raman: Regarding costs again, can the cost delta between Dedicated and Hosted be made up in 3-6 months for our volume?
11:19 Jenna Ortiz: We'll show a 6–12 month run-rate in the TCO scenarios. If you commit to Reserved Dedicated capacity, break-even is often in the 4–9 month range depending on model mix.
11:33 Marcus Lee: Ok wrapping the technical plan: inputs from Zephyr — traces, prompts, target SLAs, list of models. Redwood will run bench across Hosted (EU), Dedicated (EU reserve) and a trimmed Private sim if network allows. Deliverables: bench report, TCO sheet, security pack, SOW draft.
11:55 Priya Raman: That sounds good. One last nit — can you include an example A/B test config for canarying new model variants?
12:02 Marcus Lee: We'll attach sample rollout snippets and routing rules.
12:10 Jenna Ortiz: Great — recap of next steps: Zephyr to send traces and prompts by 2027-12-03; Redwood to run bench and send security pack; follow-up meeting to review bench 2027-12-10.
12:25 Tom Yang: Thanks everyone.
12:28 Sofie Müller: Thanks — appreciate the thoroughness.
12:30 Meeting end.
